newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosnia must take back refugees or lose aid -Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia must take back refugees or lose aid -Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel warned Bosnia in an interview published on Sunday that it would lose Western financial help if it did not do more to take back hundreds of thousands of refugees from western Europe.

But Michael Steiner, the international community's deputy High Representative to Bosnia, said there could be a new tide of refugees if Moslems were sent back wholesale to areas which were not their home regions.
There are still some 300,000 Bosnian refugees in Germany, most of them Moslems driven out of areas now ruled by Serbs.
Cash-strapped German authorities are increasingly determined that they should go back to Bosnia soon.
Kinkel told the weekly Welt am Sonntag that Bosnian authorities which did not do enough to overcome continuing ethnic animosity and make this possible "will simply not be helped any more".
He said there was agreement on this both within Germany and among the international community.
"It won't be just financial support that is withdrawn. There will also be tougher action towards the politicians who are responsible in Bosnia and Herzegovina," he said.
The paper said Kinkel's ministry had calculated the Bosnian refugees had cost Germany 14 billion marks since 1991.

Last Friday Kinkel and Germany's regional states agreed to improve their level of information on the places of origin of the refugees, and to send a German coordinator to Sarajevo to liaise between the various bodies organising the repatriation.
Steiner said 45,000 refugees had already returned and that most others wanted to but, as Moslems driven from their homes under a Serb policy of "ethnic cleansing", simply could not.
"They can't return to the Serb Republic while conditions are as they are and while (Serb ex-leader and accused war criminal Radovan) Karadzic still says what goes," he told German Radio.
Steiner said it would be a grave error to send back these Moslems anyway, forcing them to try to settle in Bosnia's other "entity", the Moslem-Croat Federation.
"We would in practice be contributing to the creation of ethnically homogenous areas," he said.
He said an influx of Moslems would endanger a delicate ethnic balance in the Federation and compound the problem of 80 percent unemployment.
"We don't want to create a situation where we would have to expect more refugee flows, most of whom would head back towards Germany," he said.

Steiner also said Germany should not keep emphasising that it had take in more refugees than any other country in the West, noting that both Sweden and Austria had taken in more relative to their populations.
